## Ingest
Quick review of different files provided. Two main datasets: 
```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
bank_add <- read.csv("../Data/bank-additional-full.csv", sep = ";")
bank_full <- read.csv("../Data/bank-full.csv", sep = ";")
glimpse(bank_full)
```
`Bank-additional-full.csv` has `r dim(bank_full)[1]-dim(bank_add)[1]` fewer rows and additional columns: `r paste(setdiff(names(bank_add), names(bank_full)), collapse = ", ")`. 

Names only in `bank-full.csv`: `r paste(setdiff(names(bank_full), names(bank_add)), collapse = ", ")`.

```{r}
summary(bank_add %>% mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)))
```

About `r scales::percent(mean(bank_full$y == "yes"), accuracy = 0.1)` of contacts in `bank-full.csv` subscribe. The rate by month is much higher in the months with fewer contacts. Bar labels are contact counts, and each month pools May 2008 through November 2010.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=4.5}
month_levels <- c(
  "jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun",
  "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec"
)

bank_full %>%
  mutate(month = factor(month, levels = month_levels)) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(
    contacts = n(),
    subscribe_rate = mean(y == "yes"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, subscribe_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(contacts)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Subscription rate by contact month",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Subscription rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Instead of using a `set.seed()` function, the authors provided samples for both datasets.

Remaining EDA should bring in the additional columns in `Bank-additional-full.csv` if macro economics seem appropriate. Macro is a would-be-nice in objective 1, and only if additional predictive power is found in objective 2.

Suspecting a seasonal trend.
